items.title: Chamath Palihapitiya: Anthropic Employee's "Human Extinction" AI Warning Risks $2.3 Trillion IPO
items.note: Published September 13, 2026, this piece reports Chamath's comments on the September 11 All-In episode that a departing Anthropic safety researcher's human extinction warning complicates the company's roughly 2.3 trillion dollar IPO plans.

items.title: Policy on the AI Exponential
items.note: Dario Amodei published a roughly 3,800 word essay on September 12, 2026 arguing AI companies should deliberately slow the pace of capability improvements and calling for independent evaluators embedded inside frontier labs, backed eventually by federal regulation.

items.title: CBS News Sunday Morning: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on AI risk
items.note: In an interview aired September 12, 2026, Amodei said AI's exponential growth is a warning sign the industry needs to slow down, and said the industry had understated the technology's risks for too long.

items.title: Grande Sertão: Veredas, de Guimarães Rosa, a advocacia e a IA que ia, veio
items.note: Jornal Opção essay published September 11, 2026 marks the novel's 70th anniversary and connects its themes to law and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Dia do Cerrado: Guimarães Rosa denunciou riscos ao bioma, diz bióloga
items.note: Agência Brasil piece tied to Cerrado Day, September 11, 2026, argues that Guimarães Rosa's writing anticipated environmental risks to the Cerrado biome, according to an interviewed biologist.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: seeing sound, hearing time
items.note: Sakamoto's first major European retrospective opened September 11, 2026 at Hamburger Bahnhof Berlin, spanning 1,500 square meters with sound installations made with Shiro Takatani, Carsten Nicolai and Apichatpong Weerasethakul, running through May 23, 2027.

items.title: Music by Ryuichi Sakamoto (Japan Society film retrospective)
items.note: Japan Society New York held a two day film retrospective on September 11 and 12, 2026, screening films scored by Sakamoto including Royal Space Force and Tokyo Decadence, alongside sales of his newly translated English memoir.

items.title: Michelle Obama gets warm welcome at US Open during star-studded semifinal night
items.note: Michelle Obama attended the US Open women's semifinals at Arthur Ashe Stadium on September 10, 2026, seated among other notable attendees including Al Roker, Hoda Kotb and Robin Roberts.

items.title: No. 26: Dario and Daniela Amodei: The Jewish siblings shaping AI's next frontier
items.note: Jerusalem Post profile, published around September 10 to 11, 2026, ranks the Amodei siblings on its 50 Most Influential Jews list and discusses Daniela's role as Anthropic president overseeing safety and trust.

items.title: Music Sets You Free: A Memoir
items.note: HarperVia published the first English translation, by Sam Bett, of Sakamoto's two Japanese memoirs combined as Music Sets You Free, with the Japan Times review running September 7 ahead of the book's September 24, 2026 release.

items.title: GPT-6 Hits AGI? Tech Euphoria 2.0, SF Mansion Shortage, NYC Bans AI in Schools & Venezuela Oil Deal
items.note: All-In episode recorded around Chamath's 50th birthday on September 4, 2026, debating whether OpenAI's newly released GPT-6 Astra model represents AGI, plus AI policy backlash discussion.

items.title: O Ovo e a Galinha, new solo stage adaptation
items.note: A new solo stage adaptation of Lispector's 1964 story O Ovo e a Galinha, directed by Joana Medeiros and performed by Ana Hartmann, premiered September 4, 2026 at Teatro Ziembinski in Rio de Janeiro and runs through September 27.

items.title: Patagonia Joins Lawsuit Against Trump's Order Shrinking Utah National Monuments
items.note: On September 2, 2026, Patagonia, the company Chouinard founded, sued the Trump administration with seven environmental and Indigenous rights groups over its July 2026 order cutting Bears Ears National Monument by roughly 91 percent.

items.title: How Smart Leaders Build Trust
items.note: Stanford GSB Insights article published September 2, 2026 features the JetBlue chairman on building a high trust organizational culture, with seven practical tips for leaders.

items.title: A Blueprint for Keeping Humans in Control of AI
items.note: Stanford GSB Insights piece from September 2026 covers research by PhD student William Overman and professor Mohsen Bayati using game theory and reinforcement learning to design oversight frameworks for autonomous AI agents.

items.title: Warning on OpenAI safety story and open-source AI
items.note: Chamath posted on X around August 30, 2026 that a report on unsettling internal AI behavior at OpenAI would be used to justify new restrictions on open source and open weight models, which he called the start of a Closed Model Industrial Complex.

items.title: Anthropic's $30 Trillion Moonshot
items.note: In his weekly newsletter, published around August 30, 2026, Chamath examines Anthropic's reported pitch to IPO investors that its addressable market exceeds 30 trillion dollars, tied to a raise of up to 100 billion dollars near a 2 trillion dollar valuation.

items.title: Sakamoto + Shiro Takatani: Ambient Kyoto, Tokyo
items.note: The Ambient Kyoto exhibition opens for the first time in Tokyo at Azabudai Hills Gallery from August 28 to October 25, featuring async immersion, an installation by Sakamoto and Shiro Takatani built around a 26.4 meter screen with new spatial sound design.

items.title: You Need to Learn to Say No (Even to an Inauguration) with Taraji P. Henson
items.note: IMO episode with Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson released August 28, 2026, featuring Taraji P. Henson on setting boundaries, why Michelle skipped a presidential inauguration, and post White House therapy.

items.title: How AI could uncover the hidden ways people work together
items.note: Published late August 2026, this Stanford Report piece covers GSB professor Amir Goldberg and PhD candidate Yankai Wang's award winning large coordination model research from the Stanford HAI and Google DeepMind AI for Organizations Grand Challenge.

items.title: TIME Reveals the 2026 TIME100 AI List
items.note: TIME named Daniela Amodei to its 2026 TIME100 AI list alongside her brother Dario, published August 26, 2026, quoting her on sibling alignment and the difficulty of balancing safety with rapid AI advancement.

items.title: Salesforce and Anthropic Announce Claudeforce
items.note: Anthropic and Salesforce announced Claudeforce on August 26, 2026, an expanded partnership putting Salesforce's CRM inside Claude via a plugin with 37 prebuilt sales skills, with a wider beta planned for September 2026.

items.title: Naspers exec pay under fire as shareholders vote against policy again
items.note: At the Naspers AGM on August 26, 2026, ordinary N shareholders again voted non-bindingly against the remuneration policy covering CEO Fabricio Bloisi, roughly 74 percent opposed, though the resolution passed due to the high vote A shares.

items.title: Michelle Obama Talks Fashion to Sold-Out Island Crowds
items.note: Coverage of Michelle Obama's sold out Martha's Vineyard Author Series appearance on August 23, 2026 for her new book The Look, discussing media scrutiny of her clothing and body during the Obama presidency.

items.title: Os 70 anos de Grande sertão: Veredas chegam ao Museu da Língua Portuguesa
items.note: On August 22, 2026 the Museu da Língua Portuguesa in São Paulo held panels with writers Milton Hatoum, Jeferson Tenório and Socorro Acioli marking 70 years of Grande Sertão: Veredas, alongside a Companhia das Letras commemorative edition.

items.title: Anthropic to Grant CEO Amodei Extra Voting Power Ahead of IPO, Report Says
items.note: Report that Anthropic plans to issue supervoting shares to CEO Dario Amodei and its other co-founders ahead of a planned IPO, since his ownership stake has fallen to roughly 2 percent.

items.title: Anthropic to Grant CEO Amodei Extra Voting Power Ahead of IPO, Report Says
items.note: Report names Daniela Amodei among the seven Anthropic co-founders, including her brother Dario, set to receive supervoting shares ahead of the company's planned IPO.

items.title: Socrates' Turf
items.note: Merve Emre interviews philosopher Agnes Callard for a New York Review of Books online series on the interview form, discussing the Socratic dialogue as a model Callard calls the philosopher's interview, published August 18, 2026.

items.title: Rio de Clarice: filme adapta cinco contos de Clarice Lispector
items.note: The film Rio de Clarice opened in Brazilian theaters on August 13, adapting five Lispector short stories through five Brazilian filmmakers, with a script co-written by her grand niece Nicole Allgranti and biographer Teresa Montero.

items.title: REG - Prosus NV Naspers Limited - Director/PDMR Shareholding
items.note: Regulatory disclosure dated August 12, 2026 covering Fabricio Bloisi's exercise and sale of Naspers and linked Prosus share options ahead of their August 2026 expiry.

items.title: 12 Conversations
items.note: Noton announced 12 Conversations, a previously unreleased collaborative album by Sakamoto and Alva Noto recorded in 2022 during the sessions for Sakamoto's final solo album 12, due out September 18, 2026.

items.title: Fabricio Bloisi: é possível criar algo grande do nada
items.note: In an August 2026 interview with Seja Relevante, a Fundação Dom Cabral platform, Bloisi said entrepreneurs who anticipate the world five years out can achieve more than in the previous fifteen, citing Movile's near bankruptcies before it became a major Latin American tech company.

items.title: Yvon Chouinard Was Destroying the Mountains He Loved. He Made 1 Painful Decision That Built the Patagonia Empire
items.note: Inc. piece published August 4, 2026 revisiting Chouinard's decision to abandon pitons, the environmental call that reshaped his business decades before sustainability became a buzzword.

items.title: Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers, not specialists, in the AI era
items.note: On Lenny's Podcast, Netflix Chief Product and Technology Officer Elizabeth Stone explains why Netflix is hiring more systems thinkers who can work across business domains rather than narrow specialists, and describes AI fluency as a universal expectation across the company.

items.title: Netflix wants 'AI fluency' from everyone, but craft is still scarce
items.note: This piece recaps Elizabeth Stone's comments that AI fluency means an experimentation mindset plus judgment about where AI helps, while deep craft in engineering, data science and design remains scarce and increasingly valuable.

items.title: On underestimating AI regulatory capture
items.note: Gurley revisited his 2023 All-In Summit talk 2,851 Miles about AI incumbents pursuing regulatory capture against open models, saying on X around July 28, 2026 that he underestimated how aggressively they would pursue it.

items.title: Temporada prorrogada: Beth Goulart, em Simplesmente eu, Clarice Lispector, no Teatro Moise Safra
items.note: Covers the extended Sao Paulo season of Beth Goulart's long running solo play about Clarice Lispector, paired with a companion exhibition, Entre Ela e Eu, in the theater foyer.

items.title: Vastlands: The Crossing
items.note: Alison Entrekin's long-awaited English translation of Grande Sertão: Veredas, a decade in the making. The first new English version of Rosa's masterpiece since 1963, timed with the novel's 70th anniversary.
